title: Ask ARIEL governed result envelope
description: The JSON wire contract for GovernedResultEnvelope. THIS FILE, not the Python dataclasses, is the cross-language contract. PRODUCER CONFORMANCE SCHEMA: additionalProperties is false throughout, so Ask ARIEL's own output must contain exactly these keys - that is what catches a snake_case key, a stray hotelId, or a typo. CONSUMERS must instead ignore unknown fields (System.Text.Json and TypeScript interfaces do so by default), because additive OPTIONAL fields do not bump schemaVersion. Version 2.0 adds three required things to 1.0 - an explicit comparison state, a governed relative variance, and a declarative presentation hint - and two further payload families, so it is a breaking change and the version moves. Three payload types are defined here: metric_set, time_series and breakdown. Only metric_set has a live producer; the other two are frozen contract shapes with synthetic canonical fixtures. holdings_position, scenario_result and variance_decomposition are named in the Python Literal for typing honesty but are NOT accepted here, because a frozen wire schema must not accept a token no producer can emit.

schemaVersion.description: The version of THIS envelope schema. Because several unrelated contracts in this repository each report a version, a consumer identifies this one by the pair (payloadType, schemaVersion).

payloadType.description: The single discriminator a consumer switches on. Token values are snake_case identifiers; only property NAMES are camelCase.

domain.description: The analytical domain. Constrained to the only implemented value - the Python Literal declares fnb, market_segments and holdings for typing honesty, but no capability in those domains exists, so the wire schema does not accept them yet.

questionType.description: The analytical operation. variance_drivers, outlook and scenario are declared in Python but have no capability and no payload, so they are not accepted here.

status.description: Governed success. Failures and empty results travel as a separate ToolError envelope ('error' / 'empty'), never as this contract.

resultId.description: Opaque result identity. NEVER authorization: reads of the persisted result and its evidence are re-authorized server-side against a freshly verified scope.

queryVersion.description: The capability's own version, derived from the trailing _v<N> of queryId - never independently hand-typed.

recommendedPresentation.description: DECLARATIVE ONLY. A single token from a bounded registry naming an intended presentation family. It carries no HTML, no CSS, no chart configuration, no template identifier and no model-authored content, and a consumer that ignores it must still render a correct result. It is deliberately NOT pinned to questionType: the two are 1:1 today, but a governed capability may later choose a different presentation for the same question type, and pinning them would force a schema break to express that.

context.description: Temporal context is TYPED per temporal model, discriminated by 'kind'. The per-payloadType branches below pin which kind each payload requires.

payload.description: Pinned to the payloadType discriminator by the branches below.

allOf.description: DISCRIMINATOR INTEGRITY - metric_set. The discriminator must actually describe the payload, or switching on it is worse than not having it. A metric_set answers a performance question at ONE resolved business date, and its context.view is non-null because view names the governed metric bundle the result represents.

DISCRIMINATOR INTEGRITY - time_series. A trend's resolved period is a RANGE, so it requires a dateRangeContext. Letting it travel on a business-date context would overload businessDate into 'the last date in the window', which is how a typed temporal model quietly becomes a generic one.

DISCRIMINATOR INTEGRITY - breakdown. A breakdown decomposes one metric across one dimension at one resolved business date, so it uses a businessDateContext. It carries no view: a breakdown is not a metric bundle, so context.view is null.

COMPARATOR CROSS-FIELD INVARIANT (metric_set only - it is the only payload carrying per-metric comparisons). comparator 'none' means the caller did not ask for a comparison, which is a different answer from asking and finding nothing. So: comparator == 'none' implies every metric's comparison is null, and comparator != 'none' implies every metric carries a comparison object (whose members may individually be null). This is what gives 'comparison is null' exactly one meaning, so a consumer never has to read the context to disambiguate. governed_result/validation.py enforces the same rule with a specific error message.

businessDateContext.description: Resolved temporal context for a business-date capability. 'kind' is the discriminator that lets other context types coexist rather than overloading this one. Holdings' as-of (snapshot) date and stay date are different semantic roles and must never share a field, which is why a snapshot context will be its own definition rather than a nullable field here.

businessDate.description: ISO 8601 calendar date. Maps to C# DateOnly. Never a relative word such as 'today'.

view.description: The governed metric-bundle selector. Meaningful only for a metric_set payload, where the branch above requires it non-null; null on a breakdown, which is not a metric bundle.

comparator.description: The comparator SELECTION for the request, not a comparison value. 'none' is absence by choice.

dateRangeContext.description: Resolved temporal context for an ordered series over a date window. A trend is not a business-date question with an extra field - its resolved period is a range, and 'grain' states what one point represents. endDate is on or after startDate; the validator enforces that ordering, which JSON Schema cannot express between two sibling values.

grain.description: What one point represents. Only 'day' is implemented; week/month arrive with a capability that produces them.

governedQuality.description: Mirrors the governed producer exactly: a partial flag plus human-readable warnings. Warnings are prose today and must not be matched on. They are GOVERNED metadata emitted by deterministic analytical execution, never agent narrative. Structured machine-readable codes are a future additive field.

warnings.description: Always present, possibly empty - never null. Maps to a non-null C# IReadOnlyList<string>.

provenanceSummary.description: The lightweight result-level provenance summary. Deep lineage - measure, mart, per-metric semantic key, reconciliation status - stays in the evidence document reached through the existing re-authorized evidence path, and is deliberately not duplicated here.

metricSet.description: The payload_type 'metric_set' payload: a governed metric bundle at one resolved period. One entry per metric the requested view declares, INCLUDING metrics with no source row, which are retained with value null rather than dropped. minItems 1 because a view's declared bundle is never empty - a genuinely empty answer travels as the governed empty envelope, not as a success with no metrics.

governedMetric.description: One governed metric. metricId is the stable PUBLIC business-facing identifier - consumers bind by it, never by array position, and never by an internal semantic key. Constrained by pattern rather than by a fixed enum: metric vocabulary is capability-specific (view bundles differ) and governed execution already rejects an unexpected metric id, so freezing the list here would over-constrain a shape contract.

label.description: Free-form governed display metadata. May be reworded; must not be matched on.

unit.description: From the governed semantic registry. Only values the metric contract genuinely produces.

value.description: null means MISSING (no governed value exists). 0.0 means the governed value is zero - a real fact. The two never collapse. IEEE-754 number: maps to C# double? and TypeScript number | null.

sourceRowCount.description: Governed metadata letting a consumer see WHY a value is missing (no source row at all) without guessing.

comparison.description: null when and only when no comparator was requested - guaranteed by the cross-field invariant above.

metricComparison.description: A comparison for ONE metric, present only when a comparator was requested. 'state' names which of the three requested outcomes this is, so a consumer never has to infer intent from a null. All numeric members are INDEPENDENTLY nullable: a present comparator value with an uncomputed variance is a real state, so a consumer must not treat this object as all-or-nothing. NOTE: no arithmetic relationship between the metric's value, comparison.value, absoluteVariance and variancePct is asserted anywhere - the projection is non-computing and carries governed execution faithfully, so a governed variance that disagrees with a naive subtraction is still valid.

state.description: 'available' - a comparator value was obtained. 'unavailable' - the comparator was requested and applies, but no source value exists. 'unsupported' - this metric does not participate in this comparator. The last two are different facts, and collapsing them into one null is what makes a data gap look like a design decision.

absoluteVariance.description: The governed delta in the METRIC'S OWN UNIT. For a percentage-unit metric that is percentage POINTS - a different quantity from variancePct, and neither is inferable from the other.

variancePct.description: The governed RELATIVE change, as a 0-1 fraction matching this contract's existing 'percentage' unit convention (+5% is 0.05). Owned and computed by governed execution (revenue_digest_execution.compute_variance_pct); no UI, BFF, MCP App or model may derive it. Null when it could not be computed, and variancePctReason then says why - never 0, never infinity, never silently omitted.

variancePctReason.description: Why variancePct is null on an otherwise available comparison. 'comparator_zero_base': the comparator value is exactly 0, so no division is performed - a zero base is a real governed value, not a missing one. 'insufficient_data': an input was missing. Null when variancePct is present, and null when state is not 'available' because the state already explains the absence.

sourceVariance.description: The mart-provided Value_Vs_* figure where one exists - only for mtd/ytd comparators. Its reconciliation verdict against absoluteVariance lives in the evidence document, not here.

allOf.description: STATE AND VALUE CAN NEVER DISAGREE: state is 'available' if and only if a comparator value is present. Without this, the five comparison states stop being distinguishable.
A NULL PERCENTAGE ON AN AVAILABLE COMPARISON IS NEVER UNEXPLAINED: if it could have been computed and was not, the packet says why.
A REASON CANNOT ACCOMPANY A PRESENT PERCENTAGE - it would be a second explanation free to contradict the first.
AN UNAVAILABLE OR UNSUPPORTED COMPARISON CARRIES NO PERCENTAGE AND NO REASON - the state already explains the absence.

timeSeries.description: The payload_type 'time_series' payload: ONE approved metric over an ordered date window. CONTRACT ONLY - no capability produces this today, and its canonical fixtures are synthetic. The payload carries NO summary statistics: no high, low, mean, range, slope or growth rate. If one is ever wanted it becomes a governed output field, never a rendering step.

points.description: Ordered ascending by date, with no duplicate dates. The ORDERING IS GOVERNED - a consumer renders the order given and never re-sorts into a different meaning. The validator enforces ordering and uniqueness, which JSON Schema cannot express across array items.

seriesPoint.description: One governed point. A null value is a genuine gap and is retained IN POSITION - never dropped (which would silently shorten the window and change what the series means), never interpolated, never zero-filled.

breakdown.description: The payload_type 'breakdown' payload: ONE approved metric decomposed across ONE approved dimension. CONTRACT ONLY - no capability produces this today, and its canonical fixtures are synthetic. reconciledTotal is stated so that no consumer ever divides to obtain a share; that division is what would make a presentation layer an analytical one.

dimension.description: The approved PUBLIC dimension identifier - never a mart column name.

breakdownRow.description: One governed category row. 'share' is a GOVERNED analytical value, never derived by a consumer from value / reconciledTotal. It is null where share is not semantically approved for the dimension - a legitimate result shape, not a degraded one, and a consumer must not fill it in.

rank.description: Governed 1-based rank where ranking is analytically meaningful; null otherwise.
